_comment: The first day's gathering: hand-placed harvest spots along the tutorial path, read by scripts/world/harvest_node.gd. NOT the real M8 harvesting loop (tools, durability, the vegetation itself) — a dozen legible spots so 'gather enough to make camp' is playable today. Positions are world metres, stood on the ground per D09. ALL TUNABLE.
_comment_amounts: A camp costs 12 wood / 8 stone / 10 fiber (data/items/buildables.json), so one full walk down the practice path and back covers it with a little over: 4 wood spots x 4, 3 stone x 3, 3 fiber x 4, 2 berry x 3.
_comment_bands: BAND-SPLIT. The nodes array that used to live here is now cut per corridor band, under data/config/bands/<band>/harvest.json, and merged back at load by scripts/data/band_content.gd. What stays here is what is NOT positional and must not be duplicated five times where it could drift. Every entry carries an `order`; the merge sorts by it, so the merged array is byte-identical to the pre-split file (tests/test_band_content.gd pins that against tests/fixtures/band_split_baseline/).
_comment_ironwood_sf31: SF31, spec §3 Band 4: the old-growth stands on the Rise's south-west flank, up the trainer road past the Burrow Warrens' mouth ([70,-140]) -- the upper Meadows, and the only place ironwood grows. Nodes here rather than in a new `ironwood_grove.json` because this file already IS where a gathered material lives: SD16's quarry made exactly this call for rootstone (`old_quarry.gd`'s own header: 'the Rootstone deposits are harvest.json, placed by playground_world.gd like every other harvest node') and a second config would be the drift that comment exists to prevent. Every position is MEASURED, not guessed -- `tools/_probe_upper_meadows.gd` (heights -3.3m to +0.5m, worst local slope 2.3-11.3 degrees over a 3m pad, all inside world_perimeter.gd's 235m ring at 149-183m out); the eastern quadrant beyond them is the Rise's own 45-75 degree rock and will not hold a node a player can stand at. `TwistedTree` rather than `DeadTree_2` (which `wood` already uses): the gnarled trunk is the read, and a second dead tree would say 'wood' at a glance. Amounts and scales TUNABLE.
_comment_models_r9_4: R9.4. Every node here had no `model`, and harvest_node.gd's fallback for that is a BoxMesh tinted by the item's colour -- so all twelve harvest spots rendered as coloured boxes. The blind critic found two of them sitting a couple of metres from the player in the spawn framing and noted they were 'MORE legible than the player', being the only hard-edged geometric shapes in frame; it listed them among the three assets doing the most damage. These are the vegetation's own Quaternius pack, deliberately: assets/environment/nature is the Kenney kit, which ships flat untextured vertex colours including a teal-green rock material, and mixing it in would trade one cohesion problem for another (CLAUDE.md, visual cohesion). The box fallback stays in the code -- it is the right behaviour for a node whose model is missing. TUNABLE (scales especially).
